title: A Reader keeps its last record after advance returns false
body:
`Reader::advance` returning `false` leaves the reader past the end of the stream. sail-317db4 settled that `position()` then returns `None` and `record()` returns an empty slice. That rule was chosen to ship `advance_to`, and it is open for refinement here.

Before sail-317db4, `record()` after `false` sliced a buffer whose bytes had moved in Stockholm and HMM. The final `advance` calls `fill`, `fill` drops every byte before `cursor`, and the last record lies wholly before `cursor`. FASTA was not affected, because its `advance` sets `done` while framing the last record and returns `false` on the next call without a `fill`.

No loop in `sail` reads `record()` after `false`. `advance_to(n)` with `n` past the end is the first call that leaves a caller holding a reader in that state. Such a caller may want the record where the stream ended.

## Options

| option | `position()` after `false` | `record()` after `false` | cost |
|---|---|---|---|
| none, as shipped | `None` | empty | one reset in `advance` |
| keep last | `Some(last)` | the last record | `fill` must keep the current record's bytes until the next record is framed |

No lean yet. The question for keep last is whether `fill` can keep the current record without copying it.

`lines::Rows` compacts the same way in its own `fill` and follows whichever rule this picks.

notes.author: Jack Roddy/424f83e5
notes.text: Decided by Jack: keep the last record. After `advance` returns `false`, `position()` stays `Some(last)` and `record()` returns the last record. Reasoning: it keeps information a caller has no other way to recover. After a failed `advance_to`, `position() + 1` is the record count, which sail-cce3b8 needs. Applies to `Reader`, `Rows` and `Readers`.
